en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll learn to say exactly how you feel and talk about the people in your life: -ed or -ing words, feelings with the right little word after them, and family and relationship words. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: -ed or -ing?
steps.text: You already know bored and boring. Let's use the same rule for more words.
steps.body:
These are **adjectives** (words that describe, like *happy*).
- **-ed** = how a **person feels**: *I'm confused* (saya bingung).
- **-ing** = what **causes** the feeling: *This map is confusing* (membingungkan).

This -ed is **not** past tense: *I'm bored* is about now. Trick: Indonesian **me-…-kan** (*membingungkan, mengecewakan*) usually means **-ing**.

A person can be -ing too: *He's boring* = he makes **others** bored. So say **I'm bored**, not `I'm boring`.

steps.title: Who feels it, what causes it
steps.text: Look at both forms in real sentences.
steps.body: The thing (a meeting, traffic, a price) is **-ing**; the people are **-ed**. In the last one a person is **-ing**, because he makes others bored.

examples.en: I'm bored. This meeting is boring.
examples.id: Saya bosan. Rapat ini membosankan.

examples.en: The traffic is annoying, and everyone in the car is annoyed.
examples.id: Macetnya menyebalkan, dan semua orang di mobil kesal.

examples.en: The ticket prices are shocking!
examples.id: Harga tiketnya mengejutkan!

examples.en: The spa was relaxing, so we came home relaxed.
examples.id: Spanya bikin rileks, jadi kami pulang dengan santai.

examples.en: My colleague is boring: he only talks about his car.
examples.id: Rekan kerjaku membosankan: dia cuma ngomongin mobilnya.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Budi is filling in a tax form online. He reads every page twice and still doesn't understand it.

question.prompt: Complete: The tax form is really ___.
question.explanation: The form **causes** the feeling, so use **-ing**: *confusing* (membingungkan). Budi is the one who's *confused*. *confuse* is the verb, not a describing word.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Dimas starts work at a big company in Jakarta next week. He can't wait!

question.solution: Dimas is excited about his new job.
question.prompt: Arrange the words: Dimas antusias dengan pekerjaan barunya.
question.explanation: Dimas **feels** it, so use **-ed**: *excited*. The chunk is **excited about** something. Remember *is*: `Dimas excited` has no verb.

steps.title: More feelings
steps.text: Now some new feeling words, each with its little partner word.
steps.body:
Many feelings need a fixed **preposition** after them (kata depan: *of, about, in, for*). It often doesn't match Indonesian: *bangga **pada*** = proud **of**, not `proud on`. Learn each pair as one chunk.

**alone** (sendirian) is just a fact; **lonely** (kesepian) is a sad feeling. **upset** has no -ed: not `upsetted`. Both **angry with** (British) and **angry at** (American) are fine for a person.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Your neighbour Dimas drove you to the airport at 4 a.m. You thank him.

question.prompt: Complete: Thanks so much, Dimas. I'm really ___ for your help.
question.explanation: When someone helps you, you're **grateful** (berterima kasih), and the chunk is **grateful for** something. *proud* is for someone's success, *jealous* is wanting what others have.

steps.title: Malu and baper
steps.text: Two Indonesian words that don't translate one to one.
steps.body:
**Malu** depends on the situation:
- **embarrassed** = something happened (wrong name, falling over)
- **shy** = your personality (pemalu)
- **ashamed** = you did something wrong (strong, less common)
**Shame** is a noun: not `I'm shame`. *What a shame!* = sayang sekali.

**Baper** has no one word: **Don't take it personally**, **I was a bit too sensitive**. Be kind: *You're too sensitive* can sound rude.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Rina is talking about her son.

question.prompt: Complete: My son is very ___. At parties he hides behind me and doesn't talk to new people.
question.explanation: This is his **personality** (pemalu), so the word is **shy**. *ashamed* is for doing something wrong, and *embarrassing* would mean he makes other people feel malu.

steps.title: Family and relationships
steps.text: Last group: how people get on, and words for couples and family.
steps.body:
- **get on (well) with** = akur (American: *get along with*); **be close to** = dekat (*close* sounds 'klous'); **fall out with** = bertengkar lalu marahan (past *fell out*).
- Couples: **single → engaged → get married → divorced**; **break up** = putus. *Menikah dengan* = **married to**, not `married with`. **partner** works for any couple.
- **in-laws** = mertua, ipar. **a close friend** (teman dekat) ≠ **an acquaintance** (kenalan).

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Rina had a big argument with her best friend.

question.prompt: Complete: Rina ___ with her best friend last month. Now they don't speak to each other.
question.explanation: They argued and stopped speaking, so they **fell out** (*fall out with* someone; past *fell out*). *got on with* means the opposite (akur), and *got married* doesn't fit an argument (it's also *married to*, not *with*).

steps.text: Here's the whole lesson on one page.

examples.id: Saya bingung. Petunjuk ini membingungkan.

examples.en: We're so proud of you!
examples.id: Kami bangga sekali padamu!

examples.en: Sorry, I was a bit too sensitive yesterday.
examples.id: Maaf, kemarin aku agak baper.

examples.en: I get on well with my colleagues.
examples.id: Saya akur dengan rekan-rekan kerja saya.

steps.title: Learn more
steps.text: Want more practice? This engVid video explains bored vs boring as cause and effect, and the British Council page has two quick quizzes with the new pairs.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kamu akan belajar mengatakan dengan tepat apa yang kamu rasakan dan membicarakan orang-orang di hidupmu: kata -ed atau -ing, kata perasaan dengan kata kecil yang tepat sesudahnya, serta kata-kata keluarga dan hubungan. Yuk, pelan-pelan.

steps.title: -ed atau -ing?
steps.text: Kamu sudah kenal bored dan boring. Sekarang kita pakai aturan yang sama untuk kata lain.
steps.body:
Ini **kata sifat** (adjective: kata yang menjelaskan, seperti *happy*).
- **-ed** = yang **dirasakan seseorang**: *I'm confused* (saya bingung).
- **-ing** = yang **menyebabkan** perasaan: *This map is confusing* (membingungkan).

-ed di sini **bukan** bentuk lampau: *I'm bored* itu tentang sekarang. Trik: kata Indonesia **me-…-kan** (*membingungkan, mengecewakan*) biasanya = **-ing**.

Orang juga bisa -ing: *He's boring* = dia membuat **orang lain** bosan. Jadi bilang **I'm bored**, bukan `I'm boring`.

steps.title: Siapa yang merasa, apa penyebabnya
steps.text: Lihat kedua bentuknya dalam kalimat nyata.
steps.body: Bendanya (rapat, macet, harga) pakai **-ing**; orangnya pakai **-ed**. Di contoh terakhir, orang pakai **-ing** karena dia membuat orang lain bosan.

examples.en: The ticket prices are shocking!
examples.id: Harga tiketnya mengejutkan!

examples.en: The spa was relaxing, so we came home relaxed.
examples.id: Spanya bikin rileks, jadi kami pulang dengan santai.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Budi sedang mengisi formulir pajak online. Dia membaca setiap halaman dua kali dan tetap tidak paham.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: The tax form is really ___.
question.explanation: Formulirnya yang **menyebabkan** perasaan, jadi pakai **-ing**: *confusing* (membingungkan). Budi-lah yang *confused* (bingung). *confuse* itu kata kerja, bukan kata sifat.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Dimas mulai kerja di perusahaan besar di Jakarta minggu depan. Dia sudah tidak sabar!

question.solution: Dimas is excited about his new job.
question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Dimas antusias dengan pekerjaan barunya.
question.explanation: Dimas yang **merasakan**, jadi pakai **-ed**: *excited*. Paketnya **excited about** sesuatu. Jangan lupa *is*: `Dimas excited` tidak punya kata kerja.

steps.title: Perasaan lainnya
steps.text: Sekarang beberapa kata perasaan baru, masing-masing dengan kata pasangannya.
steps.body:
Banyak kata perasaan butuh **kata depan** tetap sesudahnya (preposition: *of, about, in, for*). Sering tidak sama dengan bahasa Indonesia: *bangga **pada*** = proud **of**, bukan `proud on`. Hafalkan tiap pasangan sebagai satu paket.

**alone** (sendirian) hanya fakta; **lonely** (kesepian) adalah perasaan sedih. **upset** tidak pakai -ed: bukan `upsetted`. **angry with** (Britania) dan **angry at** (Amerika) dua-duanya benar untuk orang.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Tetanggamu, Dimas, mengantarmu ke bandara jam 4 pagi. Kamu berterima kasih padanya.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Thanks so much, Dimas. I'm really ___ for your help.
question.explanation: Kalau seseorang menolongmu, kamu **grateful** (berterima kasih), dan paketnya **grateful for** sesuatu. *proud* untuk keberhasilan seseorang, *jealous* untuk menginginkan milik orang lain.

steps.title: Malu dan baper
steps.text: Dua kata Indonesia yang tidak bisa diterjemahkan satu lawan satu.
steps.body:
**Malu** tergantung situasinya:
- **embarrassed** = ada kejadian (salah sebut nama, jatuh)
- **shy** = sifatmu (pemalu)
- **ashamed** = kamu berbuat salah (kuat, lebih jarang)
**Shame** itu kata benda: bukan `I'm shame`. *What a shame!* = sayang sekali.

**Baper** tidak punya satu kata: **Don't take it personally**, **I was a bit too sensitive**. Bersikap baik: *You're too sensitive* bisa terdengar kasar.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Rina bercerita tentang anak laki-lakinya.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: My son is very ___. At parties he hides behind me and doesn't talk to new people.
question.explanation: Ini **sifatnya** (pemalu), jadi katanya **shy**. *ashamed* untuk malu karena berbuat salah, dan *embarrassing* berarti dia membuat orang lain malu.

steps.title: Keluarga dan hubungan
steps.text: Kelompok terakhir: bagaimana hubungan orang, dan kata untuk pasangan serta keluarga.
steps.body:
- **get on (well) with** = akur (Amerika: *get along with*); **be close to** = dekat (*close* dibaca 'klous'); **fall out with** = bertengkar lalu marahan (lampau *fell out*).
- Pasangan: **single → engaged → get married → divorced**; **break up** = putus. *Menikah dengan* = **married to**, bukan `married with`. **partner** cocok untuk pasangan mana pun.
- **in-laws** = mertua, ipar. **a close friend** (teman dekat) ≠ **an acquaintance** (kenalan).

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Rina bertengkar hebat dengan sahabatnya.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Rina ___ with her best friend last month. Now they don't speak to each other.
question.explanation: Mereka bertengkar lalu tidak saling bicara, jadi mereka **fell out** (*fall out with* seseorang; lampau *fell out*). *got on with* artinya kebalikannya (akur), dan *got married* tidak cocok dengan pertengkaran (lagi pula *married to*, bukan *with*).

steps.title: Contekan
steps.text: Ini seluruh pelajaran dalam satu halaman.
